analysis.title: Introducing the Option on Implied Dispersion
key_insights: GS FICC & Equities desk now offers an option on the implied dispersion level, which removes the realised component from the trade. It gives clients a way to trade dispersion entry levels directly.
Dispersion has drawn growing client focus as a way to take exposure to equity correlation. The classic long dispersion trade buys single-stock vol and sells index vol.
Flows are now two-way. Clients are also trading reverse dispersion (long correlation) after dispersion entry points reached all-time highs earlier this year.
Common dispersion formats are delta-hedged vanilla options, volatility swaps and corridor variance swaps. The new option is an additional format.

The option has an option tenor (e.g. 3m) and a dispersion package tenor (e.g. 1y). The underlying is a package of forward-starting 1y straddles on a pre-defined basket, struck at-the-money spot on the option's maturity date.
At maturity the option physically settles into the full straddle package at the strike. Parties may instead agree to terminate at an agreed price, which mimics cash settlement.
Max loss for a buyer is the premium paid. Max loss for a seller is potentially unlimited. GS can quote two-way markets on both calls and puts.
ATMF option premiums are approximately linear in volatility in normal vol ranges, so the straddle package gives efficient exposure to the implied dispersion spread.

Worked example: a 3m put on implied dispersion on a 20-name basket (15 US names, 5 EMEA names) with $1m vega on each leg. The 1y ATMS straddle package costs $24,875,845, corresponding to an ATMS implied vol spread of 24.4v.
In the example the put strike is $21,875,845 (3v lower) and the investor pays $800,000 upfront (0.8v). The put is in the money if the 1y straddle package is priced below the strike in 3m.
Indicative 3m pricing as of 11 Sep: put -3v is 0.35v bid / 0.80v offer, call +3v is 0.30v bid / 0.75v offer.

vol_and_positioning: Dispersion entry levels reached all-time highs earlier in 2026 (Figure 1), and clients began trading reverse dispersion (long correlation) in addition to classic long dispersion.

Example basket: single-stock legs carry +$1,000,000 vega and index legs carry -$1,000,000 vega ($750,000 SPX, $250,000 SX5E). Single-stock premium is $43,080,322 against index premium of -$18,204,477, for a net $24,875,845.
Figure 2 shows the premium of a vanilla ATM straddle package closely tracks the ATM vol spread (shown for SPX Top50). The chart image was not included.
Indicative 3m dispersion option pricing: put -3v 0.35v/0.80v, call +3v 0.30v/0.75v, as of 11 Sep.
